questions.question: Which correction fixes: "Is the test well agonized now?"
options: A. Is the test well organized now?
B. Is the test well agonized now?
C. Is the test well organizeding now?
D. Is the tests well organized now?
questions.explanation: "Agonized" means in pain or distress. When asking about test layout, use "organized."

questions.question: Which is the best fix for: "That make the structure unclear to me."
options: A. That makes the structure unclear to me.
B. That make the structure unclear to me.
C. Those make the structure unclear to me.
D. That making the structure unclear to me.
questions.explanation: The singular subject "that" takes the third-person singular verb "makes."

questions.question: Which is the most natural way to ask about introducing a test framework?
options: A. I'd like to introduce a testing framework. Should we choose Rust or Python?
B. I want to introduce a test framework. should we use a Rust one or
C. I want introduce testing framework. Should we Rust or Python?
D. I'd like introduce a testing framework. Should we choose Rust and Python?
questions.explanation: Use "I'd like to introduce," capitalize the start of the question, and finish with a complete comparison.

questions.question: Which correction fixes: "I want you update the testing information to guide others in testing."
options: A. I want you to update the testing information to guide others in testing.
B. I want you update the testing information to guide others in testing.
C. I want you updating the testing information to guide others in testing.
D. I want you for update the testing information to guide others in testing.
questions.explanation: After "want you," use "to" plus the base verb: "want you to update."

questions.question: In today's log, what does "middleware-service" refer to in: "middleware-service is deployed on the phone"?
options: A. A backend service component running on the device
B. A mobile app store middleware layer
C. A phone operating system update tool
D. A browser extension for debugging HTTP traffic
questions.explanation: In this project context, middleware-service is a deployable backend component tested alongside llm-gateway on the phone.

questions.question: Which is the best fix for: "download the picture and store it on local, don't download it every time"
options: A. Download the picture and store it locally; don't download it every time.
B. Download the picture and store it on local, don't download it every time.
C. Download the picture and store it in local, don't download it every time.
D. Download the picture and store it at local, don't download it every time.
questions.explanation: Use the adverb "locally" for where to store a file. Capitalize the sentence start and use a semicolon before the second clause.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "现在的核心问题是把项目结构调整好,而不是靠文档把这件事情说清楚"
questions.modelAnswer: The core issue now is to fix the project structure itself, not to explain the confusion through documentation.
questions.explanation: This [ZH] line stresses that clear directory boundaries matter more than writing docs to paper over structural problems.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "不要老是问我,继续执行把"
questions.modelAnswer: Stop asking me so often—just keep going.
questions.explanation: A direct instruction to proceed autonomously without repeated confirmation prompts.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "rust的单元测试通常都是和被测试的代码在同一个文件中?"
questions.modelAnswer: Are Rust unit tests usually in the same file as the code being tested?
questions.explanation: This [ZH] question asks about Rust's convention of placing unit tests in the same source file via a `#[cfg(test)]` module.

questions.question: Rewrite as a clear technical question: "do you read CLAUDE.MD every time ?"
questions.modelAnswer: Do you read CLAUDE.md every time?
questions.explanation: Capitalize the first word, remove the space before the question mark, and use the standard lowercase `.md` filename extension.
